bihar_raw_news.title: NTPC and NPCIL to invest 1.4 lakh cr in Bihar nuclear plants - The Economic Times
bihar_raw_news.content: iStock NEW DELHI: State-owned NTPC Ltd and Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd ( NPCIL ) have signed agreements to set up two nuclear power plants of 2,800 MW each in Bihar, involving a combined investment of Rs 1.4 lakh crore. The agreements are part of six energy projects worth Rs 1,72,885 crore for which memoranda of understanding were exchanged on Friday. The projects comprise two nuclear power plants and four pumped storage facilities, with a combined power generation capacity of 11,600 MW and energy storage capacity of 36,078 MWh. NTPC plans to set up a 2,800 MW nuclear power plant at Bhitiya in Banka district at an estimated cost of Rs 70,000 crore. NPCIL will develop another 2,800 MW plant at Talhar in Siwan district, also at a cost of Rs 70,000 crore. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: “My father would be overjoyed”: Chirag Paswan on PM Modi dedicating Nitish Setu to Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: “My father would be overjoyed”: Chirag Paswan on PM Modi dedicating Nitish Setu to Bihar ANI | Updated: Nov 21, 2026 03:09 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 21 (ANI): Union Minister Chirag Paswan on Friday expressed happiness over the inauguration of Nitish Setu in Bihar, saying the bridge fulfilled a long-standing demand of the people of the region and that his late father, Ram Vilas Paswan, would have been overjoyed to see the dream realised. Reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bihar and the inauguration of the bridge, Chirag Paswan said it was a momentous occasion for him as the Prime Minister's visit to his Lok Sabha constituency brought a significant gift for the people of the region. "This is a momentous occasion for me. The Prime Minister’s visit to my Lok Sabha constituency brings a significant gift to the people of this region: the Nitish Setu (bridge)," he said. He further said that the project was a long-standing demand of residents and recalled the efforts made by his late father towards its realisation. "This project was a long-standing demand of the residents, one for which my leader and my father, the late Ram Vilas Paswan, had worked tirelessly. As this dream is realised today, I am certain that my father, wherever he may be, would be overjoyed to see this long-held aspiration of the people being fulfilled," he added. Meanwhile, BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was dedicated to the development of Bihar and that several development projects were being inaugurated and dedicated to the nation. "The Prime Minister is dedicated to the development of Bihar. As we reach the one-year mark, the 'Nitish Setu' (bridge) will be inaugurated, along with several other development projects. The Prime Minister has been committed to Bihar’s progress from the very beginning, which is a matter of pride for the people of Bihar," he said. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Bihar on Saturday, during which he will visit Nitish Setu in Vaishali district. He will thereafter inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects and lay the foundation stone of several projects worth around Rs 34,470 crore. According to an official release, the projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare, transport and other key sectors, and are aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public services across the state. The Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation Nitish Setu, an extradosed cable-stayed bridge over the River Ganga, constructed at a cost of around Rs 4,280 crore. The 19.7-km-long project connects Kachhi Dargah on NH-22 in Patna district with Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali district. It comprises a 9.7-km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads. The bridge will provide an additional crossing over the River Ganga, easing traffic pressure on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu and reducing travel time between North and South Bihar. national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI opens in Goa with 150 films from 86 countries, celebrating cinema without borders
national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opened in Goa on Friday, with a spectacular inaugural ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, bringing together filmmakers, film personalities and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. With more than 150 films from 86 countries, this year’s festival is being held under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, celebrating cinema’s ability to transcend geographical boundaries, bridge cultural differences and connect audiences through shared human emotions. Set against the backdrop of Goa’s cultural and coastal landscape, the nine-day festival aims to provide an international platform for diverse cinematic voices, creative exchange and collaboration. The inaugural ceremony featured prominent political leaders, government officials, filmmakers and artists, while international musical performances added to the celebrations. Goa aims to become a comprehensive filmmaking hub: Pramod Sawant Addressing the gathering, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said IFFI had become an integral part of the state’s cultural calendar over the past 22 years. He noted that the festival celebrates cinema’s ability to bring different cultures together and linked this year’s theme to India’s timeless philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world is one family. “Cinema allows us to experience different cultures and find the common ground that unites us,” he said. Highlighting the inclusion of Ramayana in the BRICS Cinema section, Sawant described it as a proud moment for India. He also underlined IFFI’s role in promoting Indian cinema, particularly Marathi, Konkani and Goan films, and expressed hope that the festival would encourage more young people from Goa to take up filmmaking and present their stories to national and international audiences. Outlining the state’s ambition to develop a comprehensive filmmaking ecosystem, the Chief Minister said, “We want Goa to be the destination where films are produced and completed.” He highlighted the Goa Film Shooting Act, 2021, the online single-window clearance system and financial assistance schemes for filmmakers as key measures to strengthen the state’s film industry. He also announced a vision to establish a film city equipped with pre-production and post-production facilities, visual effects (VFX) infrastructure and film education facilities. Sawant said advancements in animation, artificial intelligence and virtual production were creating new opportunities for the film industry. Goa, he added, aims to equip its young creative talent to participate in the rapidly evolving global filmmaking landscape. Truth, emotion and compelling stories connect audiences: Ravi Kishan Actor and Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan said the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’ resonated deeply with him, given his experience of working in nearly 700 films across different Indian languages and regions. He observed that audiences across linguistic and geographical boundaries connect with the same essential elements of cinema — truth, emotion and a compelling story. “A story born in one corner of the world can find a home thousands of miles away. That is the magic of cinema,” he said, describing films as a powerful medium for creating shared human experiences. Kishan also acknowledged Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership in strengthening India’s film industry and noted that India is the world’s largest film-producing nation. Cinema is a powerful expression of India’s soft power: Chanchal Kumar Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, described IFFI as more than a celebration of films, calling it a meeting place of cultures, ideas, memories and human experiences. Quoting the Rig Vedic thought, “Let noble thoughts come to us from all directions,” he emphasised that openness to the world enriches India’s identity. He said cinema remains one of the country’s most powerful expressions of soft power and provides an effective platform for cultural exchange. The spirit of international engagement is reflected in IFFI 2026 through special showcases from Russia and Spain, along with 21 films from BRICS nations, he noted. Kumar said a story from one part of the world could reach audiences elsewhere through emotion, imagination and shared human experiences. He also highlighted the festival’s focus on fresh voices and inclusive storytelling, with 52 women filmmakers and 62 debut filmmakers featuring in this edition. national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI showcases 12 Goan films, bringing Konkani and Marathi stories to global audiences
national_raw_news.content: Twelve films in Konkani and Marathi will bring the stories, people and cultural experiences of Goa to an international audience at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), offering a cinematic exploration of the state’s social realities, traditions and everyday lives. The specially curated Goan film package, scheduled to be screened at INOX Panjim from November 21 to 28, 2026, features a mix of feature films and short films. The selection explores themes such as identity, family relationships, personal struggles, childhood, loneliness and self-discovery, presenting narratives that are rooted in local experiences but carry universal emotional appeal. From an elderly woman confronting her conscience and a forgotten local hero revisiting his past to a daughter seeking reconciliation with her family and an old villager defending his ancestral home, the films cover a wide range of human experiences. The collection also includes comedies and dramas that examine changing social relationships and the complexities of everyday life. Stories of identity, family and personal discovery Among the Konkani films, Manguirish J. Bandodkar’s 30-minute Ancessao follows an elderly woman living alone in a quiet Goan village. She fills the silence of her life by talking about others but eventually realises that her gossip is a way of avoiding her own unresolved grief. Prompted by her conscience, she resolves to change her behaviour, although the transformation proves short-lived. Vardhan Vijaykumar Kamat’s Umesh, a 99-minute Konkani film, explores identity, trust and the consequences of a forgotten legacy. It follows a once-celebrated local hero who now lives in isolation in a rural village, surviving on odd jobs and carrying the burden of an unresolved past. His circumstances change when aspiring filmmakers Anton and Rohan arrive to document his life. Their investigation into local rumours and half-truths gradually reveals his forgotten talent and the painful reasons behind his withdrawal from society. As a relationship of trust develops, Umesh becomes increasingly uncomfortable with the camera. Family ties, tradition and reconciliation form the core of Prasad M. Naik’s 11-minute film Shakuntala. The story follows a woman who becomes estranged from her conservative family after marrying a Christian man from her neighbourhood. Years later, after her father’s death, she is denied the opportunity to attend his funeral. As the twelfth-day death ritual approaches, she gathers the courage to return to her childhood home, confronting long-buried conflicts and social judgment in an effort to reclaim her place as a daughter. Shravan Kankonkar’s 25-minute Purnata takes a different approach to the continuity of life through the journey of Zayo, a garland of jasmine flowers. As the garland passes through different hands, it brings comfort, hope and happiness during moments of joy and sorrow. Even as the flowers wither, they continue to touch lives, reflecting on how purpose and life carry forward even when one journey comes to an end. Relationships, memories and the challenges of growing up Suvidha Torgal Bakhle’s 16-minute Konkani film Noise examines human behaviour and recurring patterns in relationships. Its central character, Tara, struggles to move away from a troubled relationship but repeatedly finds herself drawn towards familiar patterns despite her efforts to heal. The recurring presence of an old fan serves as a metaphor for these cycles and the difficulty of changing behaviour even when the need for change is recognised. In the Marathi film Daryaa, directed by Kishor Arjun, a 25-minute narrative explores the experience of discovering the world through imagination and senses beyond sight. The story follows Aakash, a visually impaired boy with cerebral palsy who has never seen the sea and knows it only through stories, sounds and imagination. When his grandfather takes him on an unexpected journey to the coast, Aakash encounters the place he has long dreamed of visiting. The film reflects on the meaning of seeing and the ways people experience the world. Sankalp Sainath Parab’s 14-minute Konkani film Perfect Shot follows Vasudha, a young film school student whose pursuit of the perfect cinematic frame becomes an obsession with the Golden Ratio, symmetry and the rule of thirds. At the same time, she struggles with unresolved feelings towards her late father, believing he left her with nothing of value.
